chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Knowledge is like treasuries, and its keys are questioning. So ask questions - may God have mercy upon you - for in it four groups will be rewarded: the questioner, the teacher, the listener, and the one who responds to him.

key_terms.يَرحَمُكُمُ اللَّهُ: May God have mercy upon you

ai.seo_question: Who are the four groups that receive reward for seeking knowledge according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, underscores the communal nature of knowledge transmission in Shia tradition by rewarding all participants in the learning process. It elevates the act of inquiry from a personal duty to a collective worship, highlighting the interconnected roles of the seeker, teacher, listener, and responder. This holistic view reinforces the Shia emphasis on the continuous chain of scholarly transmission (isnad) and the shared spiritual merit of educating the community.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: According to the same documentation, God’s Prophet (S) said, “Knowledge is like a treasure whose keys are questioning. Therefore ask questions - may God have Mercy upon you - as four groups will benefit from this: the ones who ask, the one who teaches, the one who hears, and the one who responds to the question being asked.”
